construct: During diastole, an incompetent aortic valve permits blood to flow from the aorta back into the left ventricle, accelerating the decline in aortic diastolic pressure. Chronic volume loading increases left-ventricular end-diastolic volume and total left-ventricular stroke volume, which can increase systolic pressure; together these effects widen pulse pressure.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Wide pulse pressure, bounding/collapsing pulse, early diastolic decrescendo murmur, and LV dilation identify chronic aortic regurgitation with high total LV stroke volume and diastolic aortic runoff.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: A high-output state can widen pulse pressure, but it does not explain the characteristic regurgitant murmur and LV volume-loading pattern; reduced stroke volume or elevated diastolic pressure would move pulse pressure in the wrong direction.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The physiology must include both an increased total LV stroke volume and a rapid fall in aortic diastolic pressure from regurgitant runoff; no distractor captures both.
